newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to repay $206.61 mln foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to repay $206.61 mln foreign debt.

text.p: Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Monday the country would expedite repayment of $206.61 million in foreign debt, the official Antara news agency said on Monday.
Mar'ie was quoted by the agency as saying the amount represented high interest-bearing bilateral loans above nine percent and also export credits.
"If we can speed up these payments, we will save interest payments of more than $440 million (over the life of the loan)," Mar'ie told legislators at a parliamentary hearing on Monday.
Mar'ie said the government was in negotiations with lenders to expedite repayment of 45 bilateral loans from France and two from the United States totalling $50.58 million.
He said it also planned to expedite repayment of 18 export credits amounting to $156.03 million. He gave no other details.
Mar'ie said Indonesia had repaid earlier than scheduled six multilateral loans totalling $262.97 million and nine loans from the Asian Development Bank totalling $277.58 million.
"We have done it in October," Mar'ie said.
The World Bank has previously said Indonesia's foreign debt stands at about $100 billion.
